description.narrative: The project aims to promote inclusive growth in Tajikistan by improving the vocational, technical and soft skills and employability of youth (ages 15 - 29), women, and labor migrants. It will support (i) the construction of migration service centers (MSCs) to provide more comprehensive services to labor migrants; (ii) the construction of model "Job Centers" that will provide market-responsive training and employment services for youth and women; and (iii) the capacity development of migration and employment agencies.

description.narrative: Output/s as listed by the project staff.

Output: Access to and relevance of public employment services enhanced Indicator: At least 1,200 job seekers certified under the competency-based short-term skills training in project regions, of whom 30% are female Achievement: in preparation Progress/Status: To be implemented upon the operationalization of job centers in Q3 2024.
CBT short term skills training materials were developed in Q2 2024.; submitted to MOLME in August 2024.
In December 2024, MOLME approved the CBT short terms skills training materials. Competency-based short-terms skills training are ongoing.
As of March 2025, job center and migration service center counsellors have conducted explanatory and advisory activities on employment issues.
As of June 2025 - Ongoing. All five centers are providing competency-based short-term skills training. 264 participants were certified including 28 females in all project centers.
As of December 2025. Completed. 3,444 trainees including 1,075 female were certified and validated in all project centers Data Source: Project's quarterly progress reports, client database of the Job Centers Actual value: in preparation

Output: Access to and relevance of public employment services enhanced Indicator: At least 30% of Job Center administration and teaching staff are women Achievement: in progress Progress/Status: Job center staff recruitment commenced in Q2 2024 and is expected to be completed in Q1 2025.
As of December 2024, 23.5% of job center administration and teaching staff are female.
As of March 2025, job centers are completing the 30% female staff requirement for administration and teaching staff.
As of June 2025. Ongoing. Out of 45 admin and teaching staff in Rogun and Dangara job centers, 8 are females (17.8%).
As of December 2025. Ongoing. Out of 153 admin and teaching staff in Dushanbe, Rogun and Dangara job centers, are 37 female (24%). In 3 MSCs out of 75 admin and teaching staff 20 are female (27%) In both JSc & MSCs out of 139 admin and teaching staff 31 are female (23%). The hiring process in all centers are ongoing. In all 6 centers there are 204 workers in total (including technic staff) 61 of them are female which equal to 30%. Data Source: Project's quarterly progress reports, client database of the Job Centers Actual value: in progress

Output: Access to and relevance of public employment services enhanced Indicator: At least 400 female trainees in the 3 Job Centers received stipends Achievement: in preparation Progress/Status: To be implemented upon the operationalization of job centers in Q3 2024.
Designing of the stipend program completed in Q2 2024. As of Q3 2024, the program is with MOLME for approval.
By Q2 2025, approval of the stipend program by MOLME is expected.
As of June 2025. Ongoing. The stipend program is for all female trainees who get successfully certified after training. 12 female trainees were certified and will be paid with stipend after signing the stipend agreements.
As of December 2025. In progress. 495 female trainees received stipends in 6 centers. Data Source: Project's quarterly progress reports, client database of the Job Centers Actual value: in preparation

Output: Access to and relevance of public employment services enhanced Indicator: Three new Job Centers with design features responsive to the gender differentiated needs and priorities of job seekers developed and equipped Achievement: 2 completed Progress/Status: The civil works design firm was contracted in June 2021.
The design firm has developed the design for job centers with gender-sensitive designs. Using these designs, construction companies will build job centers with gender-sensitive facilities.
Construction of job centers in Dangara District-Khatlon Region and Rogun commenced in Q3 2022.
Construction of job center (and migration service center) in Dushanbe City was awarded in end December 2022.
As of end March 2023, construction works in job centers in Rogun and Dangara are 40% completed; and 10% completed in Dushanbe.
As of end June 2023, construction works in job centers in Rogun, Dushanbe, and Dangara are 45%, 20%, and 55% completed.
As of September 2023, construction works in job centers in Dushanbe is 38% completed; Rogun, 60% completed; and Dangara, 77% completed.
As of December 2023, construction works in Dushanbe is 50% completed; Rogun, 80%; Dangara 85%.
The Rogun and Dangara job centers were completed in Q2 2024 and fully equipped in Q3 2024. The Dushanbe job center was completed in Q3 2024 and expected to be fully equipped by Q1 2025.
As of March 2025, 2 job centers in Dangara and Rogun are operational. Dushanbe Job Center and Migration Service Center constructed and to be officially accepted/opened in May 2025.
As of June 2025. Ongoing. Two out of three constructed and equipped (Rogun and Dangara). Dushanbe center was completed with construction and is now to be equipped and furnished (equipment and furniture already delivered and to be fully installed after the director is hired).
As of December 2025. Completed. 3 new Job Centers were designed with features responsive to gender-differentiated needs, job seekers' priorities. The construction and equipping of Job center in Dushanbe (August 2025), Dangara and Rogun has been completed by May 2024 Data Source: Project's quarterly progress reports, client database of the Job Centers
Actual value: 2 completed

Output: More inclusive and targeted migration support provided Indicator: 100% of new migration service centers have gender sensitive designs Achievement: 3 (all MSCs) Progress/Status: The civil works design firm was contracted on 23 June 2021.
The design company developed design documents for new migration service centers (MSCs) with gender-sensitive designs. Using these designs, construction companies will build MSCs with gender-sensitive facilities.
Construction of MSCs in Bokhtar City and Khujand commenced in Q3 2022; and in Q4 2022 in Vose.
The contract for construction of migration service center (and job center) in Dushanbe was awarded in end December 2022.
As of end March 2023, construction works in migration service centers in Bokhtar and Khujand are 55% and 62% completed, respectively. In both Vose and Dushanbe, construction works are 10% completed.
As of June 2023, construction works in migration service centers in Bokhtar Vose, and Khujand are 85%, 25% and 80% completed, respectively. In Dushanbe, Dangara and Rogun job centers, construction works are 20%, 55% and 45% completed.
As of Sep 2023, construction works in migration service centers in Bokhtar and Khujand are 100% completed; Vose, 50% completed; Dushanbe, 38% completed.
As of Dec 2023, construction works in Vose are 95% complete and expected to be completed in Jan 2024. In Dushanbe, works are 50% complete.
As of March 2025, all migration service centers in Bokhtar, Khujand and Vose have been constructed and are operational. Job and migration service center in Dushanbe has been constructed with official acceptance/opening ceremony scheduled in May 2025.
All migration service centers were designed taking into account gender sensitive designs.
As of June 2025, all are completed. Data Source: Quarterly projects progress reports, client tracking database of the migration service centers Actual value: 3 (all MSCs)

Output: More inclusive and targeted migration support provided Indicator: At least 1,000 labor migrants in the project's target regions certified under the new pre-employment training program for the construction sector and 100% of women who apply for pre-employment training receive training Achievement: in preparation Progress/Status: The construction of job centers are being completed. Now PAG is in the process of selecting job center directors and other specialists. Procurement of equipment packages is ongoing..
As of June 2024, pre-employment training materials have been developed.
As of Sep 2024, the training materials are still being reviewed by MOLME and other concerned ministries. Clearance is expected by Dec 2024.
In Dec 2024, MOLME and other concerned ministries issued clearance of the training materials. Pre-employment training program is ongoing in Bokhtar and Khujand migration service centers.
As of March 2025, pre-employment training program is ongoing in all 3 migration service centers - Bokhtar, Khujand, and Vose.
As of June 2025 - Ongoing. 180 trainees including 13 women were certified and validated in construction sector; and all the female applicants got enrolled.
As of December 2025 - Ongoing. 3,444 trainees including 1,075 women were certified and validated in construction sector and all the female applicants got enrolled) Data Source: Quarterly projects progress reports, client tracking database of the migration service centers Actual value: in preparation

Output: More inclusive and targeted migration support provided Indicator: At least 60% of migrants reported increased financial literacy and ICT skills through pre-departure orientation with data disaggregated by sex Achievement: in preparation Progress/Status: Migration service centers' constructions and procurement of equipment are ongoing. PAG is hiring a consulting firm for developing pre-departure orientation program and a firm for conducting awareness campaign. Hiring of directors and specialists for the migration service centers is to be carried out.
The awareness media campaign firm was hired in Feb. 2924. Pre-departure Orientation Program Design and Training firm is expected to be hired by Q2 2024.
2 MSC staff each for Khujand and Vose have been hired. Selection process for other MSC staff including for Dushanbe and Bokhtar is ongoing and are expected to be hired by Q3-Q4 2024.
As of September 2024, 13 administrative and training MSC staff for Khujand, 7 for Bokhtar and 2 for Vose have been recruited.
As of December 2024, 25 administrative and training MSC staff for Khujand, 13 for Bokhtar and 28 for Vose have been recruited. Pre-departure orientation is ongoing in Bokhtar and Khujand.
As of March 2025, all 3 migration service centers are operational and training process is ongoing. The initial results of the training are being collected and analyzed. Preliminary results will be available by May 2025.
As of June 2025 - Ongoing. The financial literacy training program developed will be submitted for MOLME's approval in Q3 2025 (now pilot training is going on for MSCs' staff until the end of July 2025).
As of December 2025 - Ongoing. The financial literacy training program developed and taught in all training courses across all 6 Centers i.e. all 3444 trainees, including 1075 female trainees were trained in financial literacy and ICT skills. Data Source: Quarterly projects progress reports, client tracking database of the migration service centers Actual value: in preparation

Output: Planning and management of migration and employment services strengthened Indicator: 100 staff of the Department of Migration, Department of Employment and Labor Market, and other relevant agencies attended the training on planning and management of migration and employment services, of which 40% are female Achievement: forty percent Progress/Status: As of Q2 2024, 3 out of 6 sessions for training on planning and management of migration and employment services have been conducted and attended by more than 300 staff of MOLME employment agency, migration service and adult learning centers of which more than 40% are female.
The first training on labor market assessment was conducted in Q1 2023. The second training on planning and management of migration and employment services was conducted in Q4 2023. The third training on strengthening of assessment and certification of adult learning staff was conducted in Q2 2024. The remaining training on the use of data for analysis and reporting on the labor market, database decision-making system, operation of job and migration service centers were conducted from October-December 2024.
As of June 2025 - Meeting the targets but ongoing. Training were provided on (i) labor market assessment; (ii) planning and management of migration and employment services; (iii) strengthening of skills assessment and certification; (iv) labor market data-based decision making and operation of job and migration service centers. The total headcounts of trainees were 503, out of which 171 were female. Under the particular topic of planning and management of migration and employment services, 209 people were trained among whom 51 were female, exceeding the original targets.
As of December 2025. Completed. The first training on Labor market assessment was conducted in Q1 2023. In addition, the second training on planning and management of migration and employment services was conducted in Q4 2023. Third training on strengthening of Assessment and Certification for ALC's staff was conducted in Q2 2024 (for these three batches of trainings, a total of 391 headcounts out of which 110 were females). The rest of trainings on the use of data for analysis and reporting on the labor market, database decision-making system, operation of Job and Migration Service Centers started in October and ended on 12 December 2024 (for the last batch of training, a total of 112 trainees, out of which 61 were females). Hence the total headcounts were 503, out of which 171 were female.(34%). Data Source: Project's quarterly progress reports, client database of the MSCs and the Job Centers Actual value: forty percent

Output: Planning and management of migration and employment services strengthened Indicator: Data from client tracking surveys using the database of the new MSCs and Job Centers available and disaggregated by sex Achievement: system designed Progress/Status: Once the job centers are in operation, and after each skills training program (6-months and 12-months) are done, the client tracking surveys will be conducted.
The first round of client tracking survey will commence in Q2 2025 under the Dangara job center.
As of June 2025 - To start. The first round of client tracking survey will be conducted in Q4 2025 - the EOIs was closed on 12 June 2025 and draft submission 1 was sent by PAG on 1 July for ADB's review. Said CS package will be for post-review (sampling).
As of December 2025. The Client tracking survey firm was hired in November 2025 and the first round of client tracking survey will be conducted in Q1 2026 Data Source: Project's quarterly progress reports, client database of the MSCs and the Job Centers Baseline year: 2020 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2020 Baseline value: N Target year: 2026 Target value: Y Actual value: system designed

Output: Planning and management of migration and employment services strengthened Indicator: Skills and employment survey for tourism is available and the results disaggregated by sex Achievement: draft report Progress/Status: As of Q3 2022, the recruitment of consulting services to conduct skills and employment survey of the tourism sector is at request for proposal stage.
As of Q4 2022, recruitment is at technical and financial proposal evaluation stage. It is expected that the firm will be on board in Q1 2023.
The contract with the firm to conduct skills and employment survey for the tourism sector was signed in March 2023. The survey also started in March. The contractor has developed the methodology of conducting survey, identified the respondents and their categories and conducted several working meetings with PAG officers.
The firm for skills and employment survey for tourism sector completed its draft final report on skills and employment survey in September 2023. The final report is expected to be delivered in November 2023.
In December 2023, workshop was conducted to present the results of the survey with participation of ministries, sector representatives and development partners.
As of June 2025 - Completed.
As of December 2025 - Completed (in January 2024): Survey were completed. Workshop for seeking comments was done (in December 2023). And the final report was submitted to PAG in January 2024. Data Source: Project's quarterly progress reports, client database of the MSCs and the Job Centers Baseline year: 2020 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2020 Baseline value: N Target year: 2026 Target value: Y Actual value: draft report

Output: Planning and management of migration and employment services strengthened Indicator: Tajik version of ILO's ISCO-08 used in employment and management training, and verified as accurate and free from gender bias Progress/Status: Tajik version of ILO ISCO-08 used in employment and management training for MOLME staff, Labor and Employment Agency, and representatives of local authorities of all cities and districts of Tajikistan from departments of education, labor and economics in November and December 2023. The gender officer of the project administration group verified the accuracy of the document and that is free from gender bias.
As of December 2025. Completed. The Tajik version of ILO ISCO-08 was developed as accurate and free from gender bias and approved by MOLME in May 2022 and rectified by the Ministry of Justice in September 2022. The codes will be used in employment and training. Data Source: Project's quarterly progress reports, client database of the MSCs and the Job Centers Baseline year: 2020 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2020 Baseline value: N Target year: 2026 Target value: Y
Skills and employability of youth, women, and labor migrants for both domestic and overseas labor market improved

Each year at least 20.0% of all labor migrants are registered and receiving services from the new pre-departure orientation programs Progress/Status: The consulting firm to develop the new pre-departure orientation program was engaged in June 2024. MOES and PAG will conduct predeparture orientation programs at all centers under SEEP (in addition to the initially planned 3 migration service centers) and explore remote and/or online delivery of predeparture orientation services. PAG to initiate the selection of a firm to conduct survey in late 2026 by sampling labor migrants about whether they have received predeparture orientation service.
As of December 2025 - Not yet due. Data Source: Annual migration survey by the migration agency, Ministry of Labour, Migration and Employment. Actual value:

Labor force participation rate of youth and women in project regions (Dushanbe, Rogun and Dangara) increased to 50.0% for youth and 38.0% for women (2020 baseline: 45.0% for youth and 27.8% for women) Progress/Status: A labor force survey (2026) will be financed under the project after the MOLME requested for financial support for the survey, as recorded in the signed MOU of ADB review mission in February 2023. PAG to initiate the selection of a firm to conduct (LFS) in the project-covered districts in the second half of 2026 to help measure the outcome indicator for reporting in 2027, at project completion.
As of December 2025 - Ongoing. The TOR for labor force participation and migration survey will be ready by Q2 2026. Data Source: Annual labor force survey by the employment agency, Ministry of Labour, Migration and Employment. Actual value:

The Tajikistan National Classification of Occupations based on ILO ISCO-08 officially approved by MOLME Achievement: In preparation Progress/Status: MOLME officially approved the Tajikistan National Classification of Occupations (NCO) based on ILO ISCO-08 under decree #51 on 24 May 2022. The NCO was registered with the Ministry of Justice in September 2022.
As of December 2025 - Completed. MOLME officially approved the Tajikistan National Classification of Occupations based on ILO ISCO-08 under decree #51 on the 24 May 2022. Data Source: Ministry of Labour, Migration and Employment decree, the project's quarterly progress reports, and data from the employment and labor market department Base year: 2020 Baseline value: N
